oidc_jwt.description: Valid bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay of the same unexpired bearer access token as a vulnerability unless a one-time artifact is being tested.

oidc_jwt.description: External OIDC identity providers used for federated client authentication can be configured to allow client assertion reuse.
oidc_jwt.note: If this option is enabled, repeated use of the same client assertion is by configuration and should not be flagged as replay protection failure.

oidc_jwt.description: TOTP codes may be reusable within the valid time interval depending on OTP policy configuration.
oidc_jwt.note: TOTP reuse within the acceptance window is documented behavior unless reusable-code is disabled and the specific flow enforces single use.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of JWTs without nbf, or lack of nbf enforcement, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing nbf enforcement by itself as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: When using JWKS URL for external OIDC IdP signature validation, public keys are cached and old keys may remain accepted until refresh.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of an old signing key before JWKS cache refresh is expected caching behavior, not immediate trust-anchor failure.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin changes to external IdP issuer, JWKS URL, or validating key are intended to take effect and authorize the new trust anchor.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag successful login under the newly configured trust anchor as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Brokered usernames may be lower-cased unless case-sensitive username is enabled.
oidc_jwt.note: Lowercasing of brokered usernames is documented behavior and can make granted identity differ in case from the upstream value.

oidc_jwt.description: The requesting frontend client is not automatically added to the access token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: Absence of the client_id in aud is expected unless an audience mapper adds it.

oidc_jwt.description: Authorization codes are one-time and short-lived temporary artifacts.
oidc_jwt.note: Replay rejection of the same code is expected and should not be confused with bearer-token replay behavior.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Authorization endpoint redirect URI matching is exact and case-sensitive by default. Wildcards are only supported at the end of the configured pattern, and wildcard matching is disabled when the passed redirect URI contains userinfo or parent-directory path traversal '/../'. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, use exact registered redirect URIs unless explicitly testing the documented trailing-wildcard behavior.

PKCE method blank means PKCE is OPTIONAL, not disabled. If PKCE method is set to S256 or plain, Keycloak requires that challenge method. For pkce_skip and related I3 tests, configure the client explicitly: blank for optional-PKCE behavior, S256/plain for enforced-PKCE behavior.

Authorization codes are one-time and short-lived. The same code cannot be used more than once. Any replay test must reuse the exact same code at the token endpoint and assert rejection by HTTP status, not identity differences.

For OIDC RP-initiated logout, if post_logout_redirect_uri is included then either client_id or id_token_hint must also be included, and post_logout_redirect_uri must match one of the client's Valid Post Logout Redirect URIs. Do not treat logout redirect rejection as a session-binding bug when these prerequisites are missing.

When testing OIDC brokered login via external OpenID Connect identity providers, configure the provider Issuer field if issuer validation is intended. Documentation states Keycloak validates issuer claims against this configured value. Without configuring Issuer, issuer-comparison coverage is not established.

When testing external OIDC IdP signature validation, Validate Signatures must be ON. If OFF, Keycloak will not verify signatures on the external ID Token. Any I1 alg/key-substitution test is invalid unless signature validation is explicitly enabled.

Use JWKS URL ON causes Keycloak to download and cache external IdP public keys. Old keys may remain accepted until cache refresh. Do not flag acceptance of a pre-rotation key as I1/I3 until the JWKS cache has been refreshed or expired.

For external OIDC IdP static-key validation, if Validating Public Key Id is unset, Keycloak uses the validating public key for all requests regardless of the key ID sent by the external IdP. kid-based tests are only meaningful when a specific Validating Public Key Id is configured or JWKS mode is used.

The identity provider setting 'Essential claim value' supports regular expression format. This is regex matching, not exact-only matching. For I4/I5 tests involving essential-claim constraints, avoid assuming wildcard semantics; use explicit regex patterns and remember claim-name matching remains case-sensitive.

Case-sensitive username for brokered identities changes how external usernames are preserved. If disabled, brokered usernames are lower-cased before federation, while server usernames are always lower-case. For I4 case_confusion tests on brokered identities, configure this setting deliberately and do not treat lowercasing as an unexpected collision.

First broker login can automatically create or link users based on email/username and selected authenticators. Auto-linking existing accounts without verification is explicitly documented as dangerous but supported. For I4 principal-binding tests, distinguish mapper/flow-driven account linking from unintended identity collapse.

For OIDC broker tests using kc_idp_hint or default IdP redirect, prompt=none forwarding only occurs when the provider setting 'Accepts prompt=none forward from client' is enabled. Otherwise Keycloak may not forward prompt=none. Do not interpret missing upstream silent-auth behavior as state/session incoherence.

For I2 expired_token and future_token controls on client assertions, Keycloak's Signed JWT client authentication enforces Max expiration. The default is 60 seconds, and tokens should be issued right before authentication. Include a control assertion within the allowed age window; otherwise rejection may be due to assertion age rather than the intended claim mutation.

Numeric sentinel: Signed JWT client authentication 'Max expiration' defaults to 60 seconds when not overridden. Do not assume absence means unlimited assertion lifetime; tests for stale client assertions must account for this default bound.

Numeric sentinel: WebAuthn Timeout value 0 does not mean immediate expiry; documentation states behavior depends on the authenticator implementation. Never assume timeout=0 disables WebAuthn or enforces strict zero-second timeout.
Numeric sentinel: User session count limiter uses 0 as DISABLED for both realm session limit and client session limit. Do not interpret 0 as literal zero allowed sessions.
Numeric sentinel: Password policy 'Maximum Authentication Age' uses 0 to mean always re-authenticate before password update, not no limit.
Numeric sentinel: Password policy 'Hashing iterations' uses -1 to mean use algorithm default iterations, not disable hashing iterations. Defaults are algorithm-specific.
Numeric sentinel: CIBA Expires In defaults to 120 seconds and Interval defaults to 5 seconds if not configured. Polling tests must respect these defaults or explicitly override them.

For token exchange I5 tests, Keycloak documents a client-policy executor 'downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer' that restricts exchanged scopes to those already present in the initial JWT subject_token/assertion, except invisible default scopes with include-in-token-scope=false. If this executor is enabled, requesting broader scope should be rejected by design.

For token exchange audience tests, Keycloak documentation recommends using token exchange to obtain a token with a new audience for downstream services. A valid I5 audience-binding test must explicitly set the audience parameter and compare against client policy/client configuration, not assume original audience is preserved.

Client scopes are only applied if the user is permitted to use them. If a client scope has role scope mappings, the user must have an intersection with at least one mapped role or the scope's mappers and role mappings are omitted. For I5 scope-escalation tests, absence of claims may be due to scope permission filtering rather than secure downscoping logic.

The frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience. Do not treat absence of the requesting client_id in access token aud as an audience-binding bug; this is documented behavior.

Role scope mappings limit roles in issued access tokens. By default, new clients effectively get all user role mappings unless Full Scope Allowed is disabled or scopes are narrowed. For I5 least-privilege tests, explicitly configure role scope mappings/client scopes; otherwise broad role inclusion is expected configuration behavior.

Organization claims are only mapped when the client requests the organization scope. Formats differ: organization, organization:<alias>, and organization:*. For I4/I5 tests involving organization membership or organization groups, request the correct scope explicitly or the claims will be absent by design.

Organization Group Membership mapper is not sufficient by itself for OIDC; it only works when combined with the Organization Membership mapper in the same scope. Missing organization groups in tokens is expected if only the group mapper is configured.

For brokered organization login, automatic redirection to an organization IdP depends on email-domain matching and organization/IdP settings. If the user already has first-factor credentials configured, Keycloak may ask for local credentials instead of redirecting. Do not misclassify this as flow incoherence.
For OIDC callback and token exchange tests, the token endpoint expects application/x-www-form-urlencoded parameters. Do not send JSON bodies.
Authorization codes are one-time and short-lived. The same code cannot be used more than once. For I2/I3 tests, distinguish code replay rejection from token replay behavior.

PKCE is optional unless the client's PKCE method is configured to S256 or plain. If PKCE method is blank, Keycloak does not require PKCE even though it supports it. For pkce_skip and related I3 tests, configure the client to require PKCE first; otherwise acceptance without code_verifier is by configuration, not a vulnerability.

For OIDC request object tests, client policies are the mechanism documented to enforce request object signing algorithm and related validation. Do not assume request object signature enforcement exists unless the relevant client policy/profile is configured.

When testing I1 issuer validation for brokered OIDC identity providers, the Identity Provider configuration MUST set Issuer. Documentation states Keycloak validates issuer claims against this configured value. If omitted, issuer comparison is not documented as enforced and tests may pass trivially.

When testing brokered OIDC ID token signature validation, Validate Signatures must be ON. If OFF, Keycloak will not verify signatures on the external ID Token. Any alg/key-substitution test without this setting is invalid.

JWKS-based signature validation for external OIDC identity providers is cached for performance. After key rotation, old keys may remain accepted until cache refresh. Do not flag acceptance of old keys before cache refresh/expiry as an I1/I3 violation.

For I3 signing-key rotation tests against external OIDC identity providers, distinguish Use JWKS URL=ON from static Validating Public Key mode. In JWKS mode, cache effects apply; in static-key mode, admin must import the new key and old-key acceptance after update is the relevant oracle.

Client assertion reuse has explicit configuration. For brokered OIDC identity providers, 'Allows client assertions to be re-used' changes replay behavior. By default, a client assertion cannot be used multiple times. Replay acceptance is only a finding if reuse remains possible while this protection is expected to be active.

For I2 token-freshness tests on JWT client assertions, Keycloak documents a Max expiration for signed JWT client authentication, default 60 seconds. Use a control assertion issued right before authentication and an attack assertion outside the allowed age window; otherwise failures may reflect stale setup rather than freshness enforcement.

Numeric sentinel: Hashing iterations uses -1 as a sentinel meaning 'use the default hashing iterations for the selected algorithm', not literal negative one and not disable. Never assume -1 disables hashing iteration checks.
Numeric sentinel: Maximum Authentication Age password policy uses 0 to mean 'user must always re-authenticate before updating password', not 'use default' and not 'disable'.
Numeric sentinel: WebAuthn Timeout uses 0 to delegate behavior to the authenticator implementation, not a guaranteed immediate timeout and not disable.
Numeric sentinel: User session count limiter uses 0 to disable the session-count check for realm or client limits. Do not interpret 0 as literal zero allowed sessions.
Numeric sentinel: Rotated Secret Expiration uses 0 to mean the old secret is immediately removed during client rotation. This is not a default value sentinel.
Numeric sentinel: CIBA Expires In defaults to 120 seconds and Interval defaults to 5 seconds when not configured. Tests must not hardcode other assumptions.

For I5 audience tests, Keycloak documentation states the frontend client itself is not automatically added to the access token audience. Absence of the requesting client_id in access token aud is by design unless a hardcoded audience mapper adds it.

For I5 audience setup, access token audiences are controlled by client roles, audience mappers, and requested optional client scopes. A missing audience may be due to missing role-scope intersection or omitted optional scope, not an audience-validation bug.

For I5 scope-escalation and token-exchange tests, Keycloak provides a client-policy executor 'downscope-assertion-grant-enforcer' to restrict exchanged scopes to those present in the initial subject_token/assertion. Do not assume downscoping is enforced unless this executor is configured for the client.
For I5 token exchange audience tests, Standard Token Exchange must be enabled on the client. Otherwise token exchange failures are expected setup failures, not security enforcement results.

For I5 client-scope authorization tests, a client scope with role scope mappings only applies if the user has an intersection with at least one mapped role. If no intersection exists, the scope and its mappers are omitted from the token. Do not misinterpret missing claims as claim-stripping bugs.

For I4 username collision tests in identity brokering, Keycloak usernames in the server are always lower-case unless case-sensitive username is enabled for the identity provider, and even then the setting only affects the federated identity username while server usernames remain lower-case. Case-only distinctions may collapse by design.

For I4 first-login collision tests, automatic linking of an existing local account to an external identity provider is treated as a potential security hole by the documentation and is controlled by the First Login Flow. Test outcomes depend on whether the flow uses confirmation, email verification, re-authentication, or dangerous auto-link authenticators.

For I4 multi-identity broker tests, 'Essential claim value' on identity providers supports regular expression matching. If configured, multiple identities may match the same regex by design. Use exact values when testing principal separation unless the regex behavior itself is under test.

For I5 regex claim tests, Regex-Based Policy uses Java regular expressions against token attributes. This is regex matching, not exact matching. Wildcards and regex metacharacters are active semantics, not literals.

For I5 advanced group mapper tests on organization-linked identity providers, 'Regex Claim Values' toggles matching mode. When disabled, claim values must match exactly. For multi-identity scenarios requiring multiple values to pass, omit the claim restriction or enable regex mode explicitly; do not set '*' expecting wildcard behavior when regex mode is off.

For I3 config-change sequences involving default identity provider, first login flow, post login flow, client policies, or trust-anchor settings, admin changes taking effect for subsequent logins are by design. A valid coherence test must show stale evaluation after the change where the old configuration should no longer apply, not merely that behavior changed after admin reconfiguration.

For I2 future-token tests, nbf enforcement is not documented in the provided OIDC endpoint material. Acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf must not be treated as a vulnerability without additional product-specific evidence.

For OIDC code flow, the authorization code is one-time and short-lived. The same code cannot be used more than once. Any replay test must compare first successful exchange vs second failed exchange on the same code, not two independently issued codes.

PKCE is optional unless the client's PKCE method is configured. If PKCE method is blank, Keycloak does not require PKCE, though it may still accept PKCE parameters. For I3 pkce_skip tests, configure the client with pkce_method=S256 or plain before asserting that missing code_verifier must fail.

For OIDC logout with post_logout_redirect_uri, Keycloak requires either client_id or id_token_hint to be included, and post_logout_redirect_uri must match one of the client's Valid Post Logout Redirect URIs. Do not interpret logout redirect rejection as a session-binding bug if these prerequisites are missing.
UserInfo is called with the access token as Bearer token, not the ID token. session_token must always be mapped to access_token for subsequent verify_granted_identity calls.

When testing I1/I5 audience behavior, remember that Keycloak does not automatically add the frontend client itself to the access token audience. Audience is added through Audience Resolve or hardcoded Audience mappers/client scopes. A missing aud for the requesting client is by design and not an audience-validation bug.

For I5 audience tests, configure audience issuance explicitly. Access tokens only contain service audiences when client roles or audience mappers/client scopes cause them to be added. Without such configuration, audience_mismatch or empty_audience tests are inconclusive because the token may legitimately omit the target audience.

Client scopes with role scope mappings are permission-gated: a client scope applies only if the user has an intersection with at least one mapped role. If there is no intersection, the scope's protocol mappers and role scope mappings are omitted and the scope will not appear in the token scope value. For I5 scope-escalation tests, ensure the test user is actually permitted to use the requested client scope.

For token exchange downscoping tests, Keycloak documents a client-policy executor that restricts exchanged scopes to those already present in the initial subject_token/assertion. If this executor is enabled, requesting extra scopes must fail by design. Distinguish policy-enforced downscoping from native token-exchange behavior.

Sender-constrained mTLS tokens cannot be used as subject_token in standard token exchange. If mTLS certificate-bound tokens are enabled, do not use them for token_exchange subject_token tests; rejection is by design.

Default ACR values do not enforce authentication level. A client can still request a lower acr_values value unless Minimum ACR Value is configured. For I5 authorization-binding tests around ACR/LoA, use Minimum ACR Value for enforcement and verify the resulting acr claim in the ID token.

For step-up and ACR tests, Keycloak warns that claims/acr_values in browser requests can be modified by the user unless PAR, request objects, or similar protections are used. After authentication, the client must verify the acr claim in the ID token. Do not treat successful downgrade via user-modified browser parameters as a broker-side authorization bug unless request integrity protections were configured.

Identity provider 'Essential claim value' supports regular expression matching, while 'Essential claim' name matching is case-sensitive. For I5 claim-binding tests against brokered OIDC providers, do not assume exact-only semantics for the value field.

Case-sensitive username handling for brokered identities is configurable. If 'Case-sensitive username' is disabled, the federated username is lower-cased, while usernames in Keycloak are always lower-case. For I4 case_confusion tests, acceptance of 'Admin' and 'admin' as the same local username may be by configuration rather than a collision bug.

First broker login can automatically create or link users based on email/username, and some flows such as 'Automatically Set Existing User' are explicitly documented as dangerous because they link without verification. For I4 principal-binding tests involving external IdPs, account linking behavior depends on the configured First Login Flow; do not assume a collision is accidental if auto-linking flow was intentionally configured.

When testing brokered OIDC/OAuth providers, Keycloak may fetch user profile data from UserInfo rather than trusting access token contents. For OAuth v2 providers it assumes access tokens are opaque and uses User Info URL to obtain identity claims. Do not design JWT-claim mutation tests against upstream access tokens unless the provider type actually validates those claims directly.

Validate Signatures for external OIDC IdPs is configurable. If disabled, Keycloak will not verify signatures on external ID Tokens. For I1 tests against brokered OIDC providers, explicitly enable signature validation and configure JWKS URL or validating public key; otherwise signature-forgery tests are meaningless.

Issuer validation for external OIDC IdPs depends on the configured Issuer field. Documentation states Keycloak validates issuer claims against this configured value. For I1 trust_anchor_substitution tests, configure the Issuer field; otherwise issuer-binding coverage is incomplete.

When Use JWKS URL is enabled for external OIDC IdPs, Keycloak caches public keys for performance. Old keys may remain accepted until cache refresh. For I3 signing-key-rotation tests, only flag acceptance of old signatures after the documented JWKS cache refresh window has elapsed.

Client assertions issued by an identity provider are single-use by default, but there is an explicit option 'Allows client assertions to be re-used'. For I2 replay tests in federated client-auth scenarios, replay acceptance is by configuration if this option is enabled.

The option 'Allows Client ID as audience for assertions' changes audience validation semantics for federated client authentication and JWT authorization grants, using client_id instead of token-url/issuer-url and is explicitly non-standard. For I1/I5 audience-binding tests on client assertions, account for this alternate audience rule when enabled.

Client secret rotation uses numeric sentinels with special meaning: Rotated Secret Expiration value 0 means the old secret is immediately removed during rotation, not 'inherit default'. Do not assume 0 means unlimited or disabled overlap.

Password policy 'Hashing iterations' uses sentinel -1 to mean 'use algorithm default iterations', not literal negative iterations and not disable hashing. Never treat -1 as disabling the underlying check.
Password policy 'Maximum Authentication Age' uses sentinel 0 to mean the user must always re-authenticate before password update, not 'no limit'.
WebAuthn timeout uses sentinel 0 to delegate timeout behavior to the authenticator/browser implementation, not necessarily immediate expiry and not disable WebAuthn.
User session count limiter uses sentinel 0 to disable the corresponding session-limit check. This is not a literal zero-session limit. If realm or client session limit is set to 0, the limit is off.

Authentication session sub-session limit authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 per root authentication session, and when the limit is reached the oldest authentication sub-session is removed. For multi-tab/browser-flow coherence tests, excessive parallel auth attempts can evict older sub-sessions and cause unrelated failures.

For OIDC future_token/expired_token tests, include a control login using a valid token or valid flow configuration. Many failures at the token endpoint can also result from client misconfiguration, missing scopes, or unsupported grant settings, not just token freshness checks.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
